public_rationale: The release condition was not met under the ordinary named-model reading. OpenAI introduced GPT-5 on August 7, 2025, after the 2024 deadline. The claim therefore earns neither support nor contradiction from subsequent AI excitement or valuations. This is an unmet conditional forecast, not a failed prediction that GPT-5 would arrive in 2024.
limitations: The elapsed interval concerns the release condition; the forecast gives no precise deadline for the market response.
Treating another model as a mindblowing GPT-5 equivalent would require a different, explicitly justified interpretation.

our_interpretation: This year means calendar 2024. The dated interval applies to the release condition, not to an invented deadline for the market response.
The ordinary reading requires a public release of the named GPT-5 model during 2024, as well as an exceptional capability improvement.
The surrounding discussion could also suggest a GPT-5-level advance under another name. That alternative is not substituted silently for the named release condition.
Soon, hype and bubble burst have no stated measures or exact outcome deadline. Their interpretation need not be resolved if the release condition was not met.
criteria.support_condition: First establish a qualifying GPT-5 release during 2024. Only then assess whether attention increased and whether a broad collapse in generative-AI valuations and enthusiasm was avoided over a defensible near-term interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: First establish the qualifying 2024 release. Only then could declining hype or a sufficiently near-term broad collapse contradict the forecast. Failure of the release condition does not make the conditional forecast false.
